winning_patterns: Short 13-15 second clips with high-energy streamer reactions outperform 30-second gameplay reels by 18x median views.
Hooks that promise a specific failure or broken mechanic (crashing, physics, painting wrong) generate curiosity gaps that drive YouTube Shorts traffic.
Crediting top-tier streamers like ohnePixel and xQc in the hook aligns the clip with existing fan search intent and boosts algorithmic distribution.
avoid_patterns: Reject 30-second strip club scenes or generic car crashes with no streamer reaction, as they consistently flatline at 2-140 views.
Avoid long-form street gameplay reactions without a punchline or conflict, since they underperform against short, chaotic moments.
Do not post clips where the streamer is silent or passive; zero-comment, zero-share flops lack the emotional trigger needed for shares.
hook_style_guidance: Write Frame-1 hooks as all-caps accusations or broken promises about GTA 6 mechanics to create an immediate curiosity gap before the viewer swipes.
